themes.title: Forced account creation nearly causes cart abandonment
themes.summary: Checkout blocks users from even seeing shipping cost until they create an account, which almost caused the participant to abandon their cart entirely.
supporting_quotes: it forced me to create an account before I could even see the shipping cost. I almost abandoned the cart right there.
I just wanted to buy the thing, not sign up for a newsletter and a loyalty program in the process.

themes.title: Unclear upfront requirements cause avoidable friction
themes.summary: Password rules and delivery dates are both revealed only after the fact (via errors or vague ranges) instead of shown upfront.
supporting_quotes: It should just show me the rules before I start typing.
I had to do the math myself, and I wasn't even sure if weekends counted.

pain_points.description: Checkout requires account creation before showing shipping cost, with no guest checkout option, nearly causing cart abandonment.
pain_points.quote: it forced me to create an account before I could even see the shipping cost. I almost abandoned the cart right there.

pain_points.description: Password requirements are not shown upfront, causing repeated failed submissions as each unmet rule is revealed one at a time.
pain_points.quote: I typed a password, hit submit, and got an error saying it needed a special character. Then I fixed it... it said it needed a number too.

pain_points.description: Shipping estimate is shown as a vague date range instead of a concrete delivery date.
pain_points.quote: the shipping estimate said "5 to 7 business days" but didn't give me an actual delivery date

action_items.action: Add guest checkout so users can complete a purchase before being asked to create an account.
action_items.rationale: Top-requested fix; current flow risks cart abandonment.

action_items.action: Display password requirements upfront on the account creation form, before the user submits.
Replace the shipping date range with a calculated, concrete estimated delivery date.
action_items.rationale: Reduces ambiguity at checkout; low effort, mentioned as a nice-to-have.
